tagline: A toll road with a bicycle trail for company.
intro: The Suncoast Parkway runs 42 miles between US 98 in Hernando County and Van Dyke Road in northern Hillsborough, four lanes, limited access and tolled, through Pasco County in between. When it was designated in 2006 it became the only controlled-access road on Florida's list of scenic highways.

The road opened in 2001, and the Suncoast Trail opened with it, a paved path for walkers and cyclists along the western side of the highway. The two keep close company for most of the way, kept apart by fences, grass and in places concrete barriers, and no cars are allowed on the trail.

moments.title: Suncoast Trail
moments.text: Where the parkway crosses rivers and streams, the bridges were built wide enough to carry the trail beside the cars.

moments.title: Starkey Wilderness Park connector
moments.text: Four miles north of State Road 54 a separate 6.5-mile paved bike trail leaves the Suncoast Trail for J. B. Starkey Wilderness Park in New Port Richey.

moments.title: Odessa
moments.text: Peter Demens, a Russian immigrant who developed the place through the Orange Belt Railway and also founded St. Petersburg, named it in the 1880s after somewhere he had known in Russia.
